newsitem.title: USA: Aetna health unit to cover mammograms.
newsitem.headline: Aetna health unit to cover mammograms.

text.p: Aetna U.S. Healthcare, the health business unit of Aetna Inc., said Wednesday it will recommend and cover annual screening mammograms for its female HMO (health maintenance organization) members beginning at age 40.
Aetna U.S. Healthcare announced the new policy, effective immediately, a week after the federal government recommended that women in their 40s get routine mammograms to check for breast cancer.
The presidentially-appointed National Cancer Advisory Board last week suggested women get the tests every one to two years in their 40s if they are at average risk for breast cancer.
Aetna U.S. Healthcare also said it would continue to cover mammograms at any age when the woman's physician believes the test is necessary.
Aetna U.S. Healthcare provides a variety of managed care, specialty health, indemnity, worker's compensation managed care and other products to more than 23 million Americans.
